Register of Electors: 
The Electoral Reform Act 2022 introduced the modernization of the Electoral Register, 
which allows for a continuous update of the register.  This is more convenient for electors 
as they can register or update their details at any time, other than the closing date before 
a polling day (14 days).  Voters go to checktheregister.ie if they want to check if they are 
registered to vote or check or update their details.   
 
The Franchise Team were delighted to attend the Carlow Older People’s Council 
Information Roadshow in Ballinkillen Community Centre on the 24th June 2026. The 
Franchise Team were on hand to provide guidance, answer queries, and support anyone 
who needed assistance with registering to vote or checking and updating their 
registration details.

Management Development Programme in Hacketstown  
The Local Enterprise Office, in partnership with South East Technological University, 
are delivering ‘Hub Grow’ which is a management development programme focussing 
on business innovation. The programme commenced in June in Station House,

Management Development

equipped SME and micro-business owners with the skills to use LinkedIn as a 
structured business development tool. The workshop was led by digital marketing

Agency. This practical workshop was designed to teach women in business (owners 
and senior managers) how to create engaging content that will convert their followers 
into customers. 
 
Powerhouse Generator competition for Start Up & Scale Up companies:  
22 female founders attended this competition, hosted in SETU. The Entrepreneurs 
Academy ran an interactive workshop on how to perfect your business pitch. Following 
this, each attendee pitched their business to our panel of judges. There was one winner 
from each category including: Start Up; Scale Up and Most Sustainable Impact.

Catalyst HQ – SMART Regions 
The project has moved into the delivery phase, with weekly project meetings now 
underway to progress design, governance, and implementation milestones. The project 
construction tender was advertised in June.  The tender will close at 5pm on 20th July 2026.  
Catalyst HQ will be delivered in partnership with Southeast Catalyst Innovation Company 
CLG. Southeast Catalyst Innovation Company CLG, trading as Catalyst HQ, is co-funded by 
the Government of Ireland and the European Union through the ERDF Southern, Eastern 
and Midland Regional Programme 2021–2027.  
The Sorting House – Borris 
The construction tender closed on 26th June 2026.  
The Hive @ Enterprise House 
Funding for the Hive @ Enterprise House was approved by Carlow LCDC during June 2026. 
The project will now move to project delivery.  
Creative Europe – EU Craft Work 4.0 ALL 
The EU Craft project is ongoing with regular weekly communications focused on 
monitoring and reviewing key performance metrics. On 17 June, a Create Your Creative 
Business Voice Podcast session was delivered by Ampifi in Carlow Library, with fifteen 
participants in attendance. 
On 3rd and 4th June, two members from the Borris Lace Group facilitated workshop sessions 
in Greece, during which participants were introduced to and guided through the process of 
creating Borris Lace. 
A call has been opened for participants to attend the Academy in Greece focused on 
jewellery in September. To date thirteen applications for two in person and two online 
places have been received. The closing date for applications was the 26th of June.  
Erasmus + KA2 - Hands Across Generations

attendance. The meeting focused on reviewing progress to date and agreeing on the next 
steps to support the continued development of the project. 
Erasmus + KA2 - Digi-Text  
Six representatives from Ireland visited Greece on the 2nd-5th June 2026 with staff from 
Carlow County Council, LEO Louth, and a stakeholder from SETU & Carlow Kilkenny ETB. 
Participants were given an overview of the textile industry in Greece and visited textile

programme development session

Hedge Cutting 
Under Section 70 of the Roads Act 
1993,  landowners and occupiers of land 
are obliged to take all reasonable care to 
ensure that trees, ditches, hedges and 
other vegetation growing on their land 
are not a hazard or a potential danger to 
people using or working on a public road 
or public footpath.  
 
Examples of hazards might be dead or 
dying trees, ditches or hedges interfering 
with traffic, blocking footpaths, 
obscuring road signs, public lighting or a

As part of the transition from temporary protection, a new 
scheme has been introduced to support eligible Ukrainians who 
wish to remain in Ireland.   
 
The new Temporary Protection Transition Scheme for 
Beneficiaries of Temporary Protection (BOTPs) will be provided 
on a Stamp 4 basis and granted for a period of up to two years. 
The permission will be renewable for further two-year periods, 
with time spent on this permission counting towards 
naturalisation. 
 
It is intended that applications for the new permission will open 
in September 2026. Eligibility criteria will include: 
• Residency in Ireland for a minimum of one year as a 
Beneficiary of Temporary Protection; 
• Employment or self-employment for at least six months, with 
a minimum annual salary of €29,432; 
• Not being in receipt of State-supported accommodation, such 
as commercially provided accommodation or hosted 
accommodation supported through the Accommodation 
Recognition Payment (ARP), at the time of application.
